q: In the two-packet system followed for a stores tender, the correct sequence of opening of the bids is that:

options.A: The price bids of all tenderers are opened first, and the technical bids thereafter
options.B: The technical bids are opened and evaluated first, and the price bids of only those tenderers who qualify in the technical bid are opened thereafter
options.C: Both packets of all tenderers are opened together on the same day
options.D: The price bids are opened only after the material has been supplied

e: In the two-packet system the technical bid is opened and evaluated first, and price bids are opened only for tenderers who qualify technically, as required by that system of tendering.

q: Under a stores contract, the prices of inputs and a statutory levy rise during the currency of the contract, and the supplier claims payment at enhanced rates on that account. The clause of the contract under which such a claim for variation in prices is dealt with is the:
e: A claim for enhanced payment due to rise in input prices or statutory levies during the contract is dealt with under the price variation clause of the stores contract.

q: To verify the costs and prices claimed by a contractor under a stores contract, officers of the Railway examine the books of account and records of the contractor relating to the contract. The Railway is entitled to carry out such an examination under the:

options.A: Book examination clause of the contract
options.D: Force majeure clause of the contract

e: The book examination clause entitles Railway officers to examine the contractor's books of account and records relating to the contract to verify the costs and prices claimed.

q: A purchase order is placed for 900 units of an item at Rs 120 per unit. During the currency of the order, the Railway exercises the option clause and calls for an additional quantity of 250 units on the same terms and at the same rate. The value of the additional quantity so ordered is:
e: Under the option clause the additional quantity is valued at the contract rate: 250 units x Rs 120 per unit = Rs 30,000.

q: For a stores tender of very high value, the purchase office proposes to stipulate Earnest Money Deposit of Rs 80 lakh from the tenderers. The proposal exceeds the prescribed ceiling, because Earnest Money Deposit in stores tenders is subject to a maximum of:
e: Earnest Money Deposit in stores tenders is subject to a prescribed ceiling of Rs 50 lakh, so a stipulation of Rs 80 lakh exceeds the maximum permitted.

q:
Consider the following statements about emergency purchases of stores:
1. Emergency purchases may be made without following the normal tender procedure in emergent situations, by the competent stores authority, for reasons recorded.
2. Any storekeeper may make an emergency purchase at his own discretion, without recording any reasons.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Emergency purchases may be made without normal tender procedure in emergent situations by the competent stores authority for reasons recorded; a storekeeper cannot act at his own discretion without reasons.

q: An indent for procurement of stores is put up to Finance for vetting. Which of the following is NOT a matter principally checked by Finance at the stage of vetting the indent?

options.A: Availability of funds for the procurement
options.C: Whether the quantity demanded is justified with reference to consumption
options.D: Whether the lowest tenderer in the tender to be invited will be a registered firm

e: Finance vetting of an indent checks funds, propriety of demand and justification of quantity; whether the future lowest tenderer will be a registered firm is not a matter checked at indent vetting.

q: A stores contract provides for liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week or part of a week of delay, as stipulated in the contract. Stores of the value of Rs 1,80,000 are supplied 22 days late, a part of a week counting as a full week as stipulated. The liquidated damages leviable are:
e: Delay of 22 days counts as 4 weeks, a part week counting as a full week. LD at 0.5 per cent per week = 2 per cent of Rs 1,80,000 = Rs 3,600.

q: In railway stores management, the computerised system known as iMMS is the:
e: iMMS stands for Integrated Material Management System, the computerised system used for railway stores management.

q: Condemned and scrap stores of a railway are sold to purchasers through e-auction conducted on the:
e: Condemned and scrap stores are disposed of by e-auction conducted on the IREPS portal.

q: Unserviceable stores lying in a depot are condemned and surveyed off on the recommendation of:

options.B: The Travelling Inspector of Stores alone

e: Unserviceable stores are condemned and surveyed off only on the recommendation of a Survey Committee, not by a storekeeper or other official acting alone.

q: During a year, the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway is debited with Rs 95,000 on account of shortages found in stock verification and Rs 30,000 on account of downward revisions of book rates, and credited with Rs 55,000 on account of excesses found in stock verification. The net balance of the account for the year is:
e: Total debits are Rs 95,000 plus Rs 30,000 = Rs 1,25,000 and credits are Rs 55,000, leaving a net debit balance of Rs 70,000 in the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 2,500 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 32 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year, as given. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual demand x ordering cost / carrying cost) = square root of (2 x 2,500 x 32 / 4) = square root of 40,000 = 200 units.

q: An item of stores is classified as 'Vital' not because of its price or its annual consumption value, but because its non-availability can affect the safe running of trains. The analysis under which items are so classified according to their criticality in use is:
e: VED analysis classifies items by criticality in use - Vital, Essential and Desirable - so an item whose non-availability affects safe train running is classified as Vital.

q: The average consumption of a stock item is 75 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 8 weeks. A safety (buffer) stock of 350 units is provided for the item. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = consumption during lead time plus safety stock = (75 x 8) + 350 = 600 + 350 = 950 units.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 54 lakh and the total issues of stores during the year are Rs 3.6 crore. The Turnover Ratio of the stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance of stores divided by total issues = Rs 54 lakh / Rs 3.6 crore = Rs 54 lakh / Rs 360 lakh = 0.15.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 48 lakh, the receipts of stores during the year are Rs 1.92 crore and the closing balance is Rs 58 lakh. The total issues of stores during the year are:
e: Issues = opening balance plus receipts minus closing balance = Rs 48 lakh + Rs 1.92 crore - Rs 58 lakh = Rs 1.82 crore.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 1,250 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 64 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 1,250 x 64 / 4) = square root of 40,000 = 200 units.

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of an item is 10,200 units. The stock in hand is 1,100 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 600 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Stock in hand plus dues = 1,100 + 600 = 1,700 units. Monthly consumption is 10,200 / 12 = 850 units, so coverage is 1,700 / 850 = 2 months.

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of a stock item is 8,400 units and coverage for five months is to be provided. The stock in hand is 950 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 450 units. The quantity required to be ordered is:
e: Five months requirement is 8,400 / 12 x 5 = 3,500 units. Less stock in hand and dues of 950 + 450 = 1,400 units, the quantity to order is 2,100 units.

q: A depot holds 400 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 26 per unit. A fresh receipt of 200 units is taken into stock at Rs 41 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item after the fresh receipt is:
e: Revised average rate = (400 x Rs 26 + 200 x Rs 41) / 600 = (Rs 10,400 + Rs 8,200) / 600 = Rs 18,600 / 600 = Rs 31 per unit.

q: A depot holds 900 units of an item whose book rate is revised from Rs 75 to Rs 68 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: The fall in book rate is Rs 75 - Rs 68 = Rs 7 per unit. On 900 units in hand the stock value falls by 900 x Rs 7 = Rs 6,300, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: The Purchase Suspense account of a railway opens with a credit balance of Rs 5 lakh. During the month, bills amounting to Rs 44 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 47 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance of the account is:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 8 lakh
options.B: A credit balance of Rs 5 lakh
options.C: A credit balance of Rs 8 lakh
options.D: A debit balance of Rs 3 lakh

e: Purchase Suspense is credited with material received and debited with bills paid: opening credit Rs 5 lakh + Rs 47 lakh - Rs 44 lakh = credit balance of Rs 8 lakh.

q: Advance payment up to 98 per cent is made on a stores bill of Rs 12,50,000 against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, as stipulated. The amount of the advance payment is:
e: Advance payment at 98 per cent of Rs 12,50,000 = Rs 12,25,000, admissible against the inspection certificate and despatch documents as stipulated.

q: A stores contract provides for liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week or part of a week of delay, as stipulated in the contract. Stores of the value of Rs 6,40,000 are supplied 2 weeks late. The liquidated damages leviable are:
e: LD for 2 weeks at 0.5 per cent per week = 1 per cent of the value in arrear of Rs 6,40,000 = Rs 6,400.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 1.10 crore and the closing balance is Rs 70 lakh. The average stock held during the year is:
e: Average stock held = (opening balance + closing balance) / 2 = (Rs 1.10 crore + Rs 70 lakh) / 2 = Rs 1.80 crore / 2 = Rs 90 lakh.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 65 lakh. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 16 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual inventory carrying cost = 16 per cent of the average stock value of Rs 65 lakh = Rs 10.40 lakh.

q: During stock verification, 36 units of an item are found in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 375 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Excess found on stock verification is taken into stock at book rate through the Stock Adjustment Account: 36 units x Rs 375 = Rs 13,500.

q: A stores depot issues 475 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 84 per unit to a consuming department. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Issues are debited to the consuming department at book rate: 475 units x Rs 84 per unit = Rs 39,900.

q: A depot issues 150 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 320 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 9 per cent of the book value, as given in the conditions of issue. The total amount recoverable from the outside party is:
e: Book value is 150 x Rs 320 = Rs 48,000. Adding departmental charges at 9 per cent, Rs 4,320, the total recoverable is Rs 52,320.

q: A supplier defaults on a purchase order for 900 units at Rs 95 per unit, and the Railway makes a risk purchase of the same quantity at Rs 112 per unit after cancelling the original order for the defaulted quantity and giving due notice to the supplier. The excess cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Excess cost of risk purchase = (Rs 112 - Rs 95) x 900 units = Rs 17 x 900 = Rs 15,300, recoverable from the defaulting supplier after due notice and cancellation.

q: An imported stores item is invoiced at Rs 5,60,000. The freight paid on it is Rs 44,000, the insurance premium Rs 11,000 and the customs duty Rs 65,000. The value at which the item is taken into stock in the priced accounts (its landed cost) is:
e: Landed cost includes invoice price, freight, insurance and customs duty: Rs 5,60,000 + Rs 44,000 + Rs 11,000 + Rs 65,000 = Rs 6,80,000.

q: Eight wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 3 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 650 per wagon per day, as given. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Demurrage = 8 wagons x 3 days x Rs 650 per wagon per day = Rs 15,600 for detention beyond the free time allowed.

q: A purchaser of a scrap lot delays lifting the material for 7 days beyond the delivery period allowed to him. Ground rent is leviable at Rs 525 per day for the period of delay, as per the conditions of sale given to him. The ground rent payable by him is:
e: Ground rent for delayed lifting = 7 days x Rs 525 per day = Rs 3,675, as per the conditions of sale.

q: The average consumption of an item is 110 units per week, the lead time is 6 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock is 340 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = consumption during lead time plus safety stock = (110 x 6) + 340 = 660 + 340 = 1,000 units.

q: The re-order level of a stock item is 1,480 units. Its average consumption is 120 units per week and the average lead time is 7 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum stock level = re-order level minus (average consumption x average lead time) = 1,480 - (120 x 7) = 1,480 - 840 = 640 units.

q: The re-order level of a stock item is 1,050 units and its re-order quantity is 750 units. The minimum consumption of the item is 55 units per week and the minimum lead time is 6 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,050 + 750 - (55 x 6) = 1,800 - 330 = 1,470 units.

q: The average consumption of a stock item is 85 units per day and the lead time for its emergency procurement, as given, is 4 days. The danger level of the item is:
e: Danger level = average consumption x lead time for emergency procurement = 85 units per day x 4 days = 340 units.

q: During a period, a depot receives 180 demands for a stock item and is able to meet 153 of them in full from the stock in hand, the remaining demands being cases of stock-out. The service level of the item for the period is:
e: Service level = demands met in full from stock divided by total demands = 153 / 180 x 100 = 85 per cent.

q: During a year, the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway is debited with Rs 78,000 on account of shortages found in stock verification and Rs 22,000 on account of downward revisions of book rates, and credited with Rs 64,000 on account of excesses found in stock verification. The net balance of the account for the year is:
e: Total debits are Rs 78,000 plus Rs 22,000 = Rs 1,00,000 and credits are Rs 64,000, leaving a net debit balance of Rs 36,000 in the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 75 lakh. In its Stores Budget for the year, the anticipated debits (value of stores to be purchased and received) are Rs 2.85 crore and the anticipated credits (value of stores to be issued and sold) are Rs 2.70 crore. The closing balance of stores anticipated at the end of the year is:
e: Anticipated closing balance = opening balance + anticipated debits - anticipated credits = Rs 75 lakh + Rs 2.85 crore - Rs 2.70 crore = Rs 90 lakh.

q: A field official holds a stores imprest of a fixed quantity of 750 units of an item. At the time of replenishment he holds 290 units on hand and renders an account of consumption of 460 units. The quantity to be supplied to him in replenishment is:
e: In a fixed-quantity imprest, replenishment equals the quantity consumed and accounted for, here 460 units, restoring the imprest to its fixed level.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 8,400 units and the quantity ordered each time (Economic Order Quantity), as given, is 700 units. The cost of placing one order, as given, is Rs 85. The total ordering cost incurred during the year is:
e: Number of orders per year = 8,400 / 700 = 12. Total ordering cost = 12 x Rs 85 = Rs 1,020.

q: An item has an annual consumption of 1,650 units and its book rate is Rs 280 per unit. For the purposes of ABC analysis, the annual consumption value of the item is:
e: Annual consumption value for ABC analysis = annual consumption x book rate = 1,650 units x Rs 280 = Rs 4,62,000.

q: A stores contract is placed at the rate of Rs 520 per unit and contains a fall clause. During the currency of the contract, the supplier sells the same item to another buyer at Rs 495 per unit. The rate payable by the Railway for supplies under its contract is:
e: Under the fall clause, if the supplier sells the same item to another buyer at a lower rate during the contract, that lower rate of Rs 495 per unit applies to the Railway contract also.

q: In the procurement of a stock item, the time taken in processing the demand and placing the order is 5 weeks and the supplier's delivery period is 9 weeks. The total lead time involved in the procurement of the item is:
e: Total lead time = internal processing time plus supplier delivery period = 5 weeks + 9 weeks = 14 weeks.

q: In the replenishment cycle of a stock item, the portion of the stock which is regularly consumed between two successive receipts of the item and is replenished by each fresh receipt is known as its:
e: Cycle stock is the portion of stock regularly consumed between two successive receipts and replenished by each fresh receipt, unlike buffer or insurance stock held for contingencies.

q: A depot clerk has to find, at one place, the Price Ledger number, the description and unit, and the current book rate of every stores item stocked on the railway. The publication he refers to for this purpose is the:
e: The Priced Vocabulary of stores lists at one place the Price Ledger number, description, unit and current book rate of every stores item stocked on the railway.

q: The stores items of a depot are grouped as High, Medium and Low solely according to the price of each unit, the annual consumption of the items not being taken into account for this grouping. This classification of inventory is the:
e: HML analysis classifies items as High, Medium and Low solely by unit price, without reference to annual consumption value.

q: An item of stores can be obtained only with difficulty, the sources for it being few and its supply uncertain. In the inventory classification which groups items according to the ease with which they can be obtained, such an item falls in the 'Difficult' group. This classification is the:
e: SDE analysis classifies items by ease of procurement - Scarce, Difficult and Easy - so an item obtainable only with difficulty from few and uncertain sources falls in the Difficult group.

q: A stores organisation so arranges its supplies that the material arrives just as it is needed for use, the inventory held in the depots being thereby kept to the minimum. This approach to inventory management is known as:
e: Just-in-Time procurement arranges supplies to arrive just as they are needed for use, keeping depot inventory to the minimum.

q: A team examines a stores item, studies the function which the item performs, and identifies elements of cost which can be eliminated without impairing the quality or utility of the item, so that the cost of procuring it is reduced. The technique being applied by the team is:
e: Value Analysis studies the function of an item and eliminates elements of cost that can be removed without impairing its quality or utility, thereby reducing procurement cost.

q: Stores supplied under a contract are found defective, but the defect is noticed and a claim on the supplier is lodged for the first time three months after the expiry of the warranty period stipulated in the contract. The correct position in regard to the claim is that:

options.A: The claim is maintainable at any time, the warranty period being immaterial
options.B: The claim is to be decided personally by the depot storekeeper
options.C: The supplier must replace the stores in all cases, whenever the defect is noticed
options.D: The claim is not maintainable, a warranty claim being required to be lodged within the warranty period stipulated in the contract

e: A warranty claim must be lodged within the warranty period stipulated in the contract; a defect first claimed three months after its expiry makes the claim not maintainable.

q: A stores contract is placed on 'firm price' terms. During the currency of the contract, the supplier demands payment at enhanced rates on the ground that market prices have risen since the order was placed. The correct position is that:

options.A: The contracted rates remain firm throughout the currency of the contract and the demand for enhanced rates is not admissible
options.B: The Railway must pay at the market rate prevailing on the date of supply
options.C: The price variation clause applies automatically to every stores contract
options.D: The depot storekeeper may allow a reasonable increase in the rates

e: Under a firm price contract the contracted rates remain firm throughout its currency, so a demand for enhanced rates due to a later rise in market prices is not admissible.

q: Material rejected at a depot is not removed by the supplier within the stipulated period allowed to him for its removal. In regard to the rejected material so left in the depot, the correct position is that it:

options.A: Becomes the personal property of the storekeeper
options.B: Is automatically accepted into stock on the expiry of the period
options.C: Is liable to storage/ground charges and may ultimately be disposed of at the supplier's risk, as per the conditions of contract
options.D: Is issued free of cost to the user department

e: Rejected material not removed by the supplier within the stipulated period is liable to storage or ground charges and may ultimately be disposed of at the supplier's risk under the contract conditions.

q: A supplier supplies a quantity of stores in excess of the quantity ordered in the purchase order, the excess being beyond any tolerance permitted under the contract, and claims payment for the entire quantity supplied. In regard to the excess quantity, the correct position is that it:

options.A: Must be paid for at double the contract rate
options.B: Is liable to be rejected and, in any case, is not paid for unless the excess quantity is accepted by the competent authority
options.C: Is taken into stock free of cost as a gift from the supplier
options.D: Is credited to the personal account of the depot officer

e: Quantity supplied in excess of the order, beyond permitted tolerance, is liable to be rejected and is not paid for unless the excess is accepted by the competent authority.

q: A supplier is unable to perform a stores contract because unprecedented floods have destroyed his works and made supply impossible, the failure being due to events beyond his control. The clause of the contract under which he is relieved from liability for such failure to perform is the:
e: The force majeure clause relieves a supplier from liability where failure to perform is due to events beyond his control, such as unprecedented floods destroying his works.

q: The recommendations made by a Stores Tender Committee in a purchase case are placed before the Tender Accepting Authority, who is inclined to take a view different from that recommended by the committee. The correct position is that the Tender Accepting Authority:

options.A: May differ from the recommendations of the committee, for reasons to be recorded, the recommendations being recommendatory in nature
options.B: Must accept the recommendations of the committee in every case
options.C: Need not place the recommendations of the committee on record at all
options.D: May differ from the recommendations only with the consent of the lowest tenderer

e: Tender Committee recommendations are recommendatory in nature, so the Tender Accepting Authority may differ from them for reasons to be recorded.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores which have a limited shelf life, such as rubber goods and paints, must be consumed before their shelf life expires, as they deteriorate with the passage of time.
2. Issues of stores from stock are ordinarily made on the first-in-first-out basis, the oldest stock being issued first, so as to prevent deterioration and obsolescence.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: stores with limited shelf life must be consumed before expiry as they deteriorate with time, and issues are ordinarily made first-in-first-out so the oldest stock is used first.

q: A stores item is to be stocked in a depot for the first time. Before the item is stocked, it is necessary to:

options.A: Obtain a Proprietary Article Certificate for the item
options.B: Allot it a PL number and fix its AAC and stock limits, so that it can be stocked and accounted for
options.C: Hold an e-auction for the purchase of the item
options.D: Sell off the entire old stock of the depot

e: Before an item is stocked for the first time, a PL number must be allotted to it and its AAC and stock limits fixed, so that it can be stocked and accounted for.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway at the end of a year is Rs 36 lakh and the total issues of stores during the year are Rs 240 lakh. The Turnover Ratio of stores for the year is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance divided by total issues = Rs 36 lakh / Rs 240 lakh = 0.15.

q: At the close of a month, a depot has received and taken into stock material worth Rs 18 lakh against certain purchase orders, but the suppliers' bills for that material have not yet been paid. This position is reflected under Purchase Suspense as a:

options.A: Debit balance, because the bills have been paid in advance
options.B: Nil balance, because receipt of material closes the suspense
options.C: Credit balance, because material has been received but bills are not yet paid

e: Material received and taken into stock but not yet paid for gives a credit balance under Purchase Suspense, which is cleared when the supplier's bill is paid.

q: A purchaser has deposited the full sale value of a lot of scrap with the Railway, but the scrap has not yet been delivered to him. Until delivery is effected, the outstanding position under Sales Suspense is a:

options.B: Credit balance representing the sale value deposited by the purchaser, pending delivery
options.D: Nil balance, because the sale is complete on deposit

e: The purchaser's deposit is held as a liability pending delivery: Sales Suspense is credited when the sale value is deposited, so the outstanding position is a credit balance representing the sale value deposited by the purchaser.

q: An item in a depot has not been issued at all during the last 24 months, and on review it is also not expected to be required during the next 24 months. The item is correctly classified as:
e: Stores not issued at all during the last 24 months and not expected to be required during the next 24 months are classified as dead surplus stores.

q: In an ABC analysis of a depot, Item X has an annual consumption value of Rs 9 lakh, Item Y of Rs 1.2 lakh and Item Z of Rs 30,000. Item X, having the highest annual consumption value, will ordinarily fall in:
e: ABC analysis ranks items by annual consumption value, so Item X with the highest value of Rs 9 lakh falls in the A category needing the closest control.

q: A purchase section wishes to classify items not by what they cost the depot each year but by how critically their non-availability would affect work. The analysis suited to this purpose is:

options.A: ABC analysis, based on annual consumption value
options.B: FSN analysis, based on rate of movement
options.C: VED analysis, based on criticality in use
options.D: EOQ analysis, based on ordering cost

e: VED analysis is based on criticality in use - Vital, Essential and Desirable - and is therefore the analysis suited to classification by effect of non-availability, not by cost.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 8,000 units, the cost of placing one order is Rs 50 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 5 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 8,000 x 50 / 5) = square root of 1,60,000 = 400 units.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 90 units per week and the maximum lead time for its procurement is 7 weeks. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level is fixed at maximum consumption during the maximum lead time: 90 units per week x 7 weeks = 630 units.

q: The average consumption of an item is 60 units per week. Its average lead time is 5 weeks, but the lead time may extend up to 8 weeks. The safety stock required against lead-time variation alone is:
e: Safety stock against lead-time variation alone = average consumption x (maximum minus average lead time) = 60 x (8 - 5) = 180 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,200 units and the re-order quantity is 900 units. The minimum consumption is 25 units per week and the minimum lead time is 4 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,200 + 900 - (25 x 4) = 2,100 - 100 = 2,000 units.

q: The AAC of an item is 7,200 units. The stock in hand is 800 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 400 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Stock in hand plus dues = 800 + 400 = 1,200 units. Monthly consumption is 7,200 / 12 = 600 units, so coverage is 1,200 / 600 = two months.

q: The AAC of an item is 9,000 units and coverage for four months is to be provided. The stock in hand is 650 units and the dues are 350 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Four months requirement is 9,000 / 12 x 4 = 3,000 units. Less stock in hand and dues of 650 + 350 = 1,000 units, the quantity to order is 2,000 units.

q: A depot holds 400 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 25 per unit. A fresh receipt of 200 units is taken into stock at Rs 40 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item is:
e: Revised average rate = (400 x Rs 25 + 200 x Rs 40) / 600 = (Rs 10,000 + Rs 8,000) / 600 = Rs 18,000 / 600 = Rs 30 per unit.

q: A depot holds 1,500 units of an item whose book rate is revised from Rs 70 to Rs 64 per unit, the difference being adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand is:
e: The fall in book rate is Rs 70 - Rs 64 = Rs 6 per unit. On 1,500 units the stock value falls by 1,500 x Rs 6 = Rs 9,000, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A supplier's stores bill amounts to Rs 6,50,000 and advance payment is to be made against the inspection certificate and despatch documents. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value is:
e: Advance payment at 98 per cent of Rs 6,50,000 = Rs 6,37,000, admissible against the inspection certificate and despatch documents.

q: A supplier delivers stores valued at Rs 2,50,000 eight weeks after the stipulated delivery date. At the contract rate of liquidated damages of 0.5 per cent per week of delay on the value of the stores in arrear, the recovery from the supplier works out to:
e: LD at 0.5 per cent per week for 8 weeks = 4 per cent of the value in arrear of Rs 2,50,000 = Rs 10,000.

q: The value of a stores contract is Rs 45 lakh. The maximum liquidated damages recoverable under the contract, at the ceiling of 10 per cent of the contract value, is:
e: Liquidated damages are capped at 10 per cent of the contract value: 10 per cent of Rs 45 lakh = Rs 4.5 lakh.

q: A supplier fails to supply 800 units of stores contracted at Rs 60 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 75 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = (Rs 75 - Rs 60) x 800 units = Rs 15 x 800 = Rs 12,000, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: A depot issues 300 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 40 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges of Rs 1,500 are leviable on the issue. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Book value of the issue is 300 x Rs 40 = Rs 12,000. Adding departmental charges of Rs 1,500, the total recoverable from the outside party is Rs 13,500.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A stock sheet is prepared where stock verification discloses an excess of physical balance over book balance, and not only where a shortage is found.
2. A shortage found in stock verification is recovered from the stockholder.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: a stock sheet is prepared for an excess as well as for a shortage found on verification, and a shortage is recovered from the stockholder responsible.

q: During stock verification, the Assistant Stock Verifier notices that issues have repeatedly been made without proper issue notes, although the physical balances agree with the books. This procedural irregularity is brought out through a:
e: Procedural irregularities noticed during stock verification, such as issues made without proper issue notes, are brought out through the narrative report of the stock verifier.

q: A field official holding imprest stores has consumed part of the stock on day-to-day petty requirements and seeks replenishment of the imprest. The replenishment is made on the basis of:

options.A: A fresh open tender for the quantity consumed
options.B: The half-yearly Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts
options.C: The account of consumption rendered by the imprest holder
options.D: The narrative report of the Inspector of Stores Accounts

e: Imprest replenishment is made on the basis of the account of consumption rendered by the imprest holder for the stores consumed on petty day-to-day requirements.

q: Stores returned by a workshop to a depot are found, on examination, to be unfit for immediate issue but capable of being made serviceable again after attention in a workshop. Such returned stores are classified as:
e: Returned stores unfit for immediate issue but capable of being made serviceable after workshop attention are classified as repairable stores, not scrap.

q: Stores are transferred from one depot of a railway to another depot of the same railway against a transfer order. The transferred stores are priced at:

options.A: The current market price at the receiving depot
options.B: The rate quoted in the latest tender for the item
options.C: A rate fixed by the receiving depot officer
options.D: The book value of the material

e: Stores transferred between depots of the same railway against a transfer order are priced at the book value of the material, not at market or tender rates.

q: The priced accounts of stores are distinguished from the custody accounts of stores in that the priced accounts:

options.A: Record both quantities and values and are maintained by the Accounts Department
options.B: Record quantities only and are maintained by the stock holder at the bins
options.C: Are maintained by the supplier of the material
options.D: Record values only, without any quantities

e: Priced accounts record both quantities and values and are maintained by the Accounts Department, unlike custody accounts which record quantities only with the stock holder.

q: A half-yearly statement is prepared to prove that the balances of the Priced Stores Ledger agree with the balances in the general books of the railway, covering stock as well as stores suspense heads. This statement is the:
e: The Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts is the half-yearly statement proving agreement between the Priced Stores Ledger balances and the general books, covering stock and stores suspense heads.

q: Each stores depot prepares a monthly summary of its stores transactions, showing receipts and issues, and sends it for compilation of the stores accounts. This document is the:
e: The Stores Monthly Summary (SMS) is prepared by each depot monthly, showing its receipts and issues, and is sent for compilation of the stores accounts.

q: A railway office requires common-use office goods which are listed by sellers on a national online marketplace for Government buyers. The portal meant for such procurement is:
e: Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is the national online portal for procurement of common-use goods and services listed by sellers for Government buyers.

q: In a stores tender invited under the two-packet system, the techno-commercial evaluation is completed first. The price packets are then opened:

options.A: Only of those bidders who have qualified in the techno-commercial bid
options.B: Of all bidders, whether qualified or not
options.C: Before the techno-commercial packets are opened
options.D: Only after negotiations with all bidders are over

e: In the two-packet system, price packets are opened only of bidders who have qualified in the techno-commercial evaluation.

q: During the currency of a stores contract, it is found that the contractor has sold the same item to another buyer at a rate lower than the rate in the railway contract. Under the fall clause of the contract:

options.A: The railway contract stands automatically cancelled
options.B: The lower rate shall apply to the railway contract also
options.C: The contractor must stop supplying the Railway
options.D: The Railway must pay the higher contract rate in all cases

e: Under the fall clause, a lower rate at which the contractor sells the same item to another buyer during the contract applies to the railway contract also.

q: During the currency of a purchase order, a depot develops an urgent additional requirement of the same item and the purchase office orders a further quantity from the same firm on the same rates, terms and conditions. This is permissible under the:
e: A further quantity ordered from the same firm on the same rates, terms and conditions during the currency of a purchase order is permissible under the option clause.

q: Stores supplied under a contract are found defective while still within the warranty period stipulated in the contract. Under the warranty clause, the supplier is required to:

options.A: Take back the defective stores without any further obligation
options.B: Supply fresh stores only against a new purchase order
options.C: Repair the defective stores at the Railway's cost
options.D: Replace or repair the defective stores free of cost

e: Under the warranty clause, stores found defective within the warranty period must be replaced or repaired by the supplier free of cost.

q: A quantity of unserviceable stores lying in a depot is to be condemned and surveyed off before it can be sold as scrap. The condemnation is done on the recommendation of a:

options.D: Supplier who originally supplied the stores

e: Unserviceable stores are condemned and surveyed off before disposal as scrap only on the recommendation of a Survey Committee.

q: A lot of scrap is knocked down in an e-auction and the purchaser has paid the earnest money. The balance of the sale value is payable by the purchaser within:
e: Under the IREPS e-auction conditions of sale, the balance sale value of a depot scrap lot is payable within 10 days of acceptance of the bid; the 40-day period is the free time allowed for taking delivery, not for payment.

q: A purchaser of scrap has paid the full sale value but does not lift the material within the stipulated delivery period, and the material continues to occupy railway premises. For the period of delay in lifting, the purchaser is liable to pay:

options.A: Liquidated damages to the depot storekeeper

e: A scrap purchaser who delays lifting the material beyond the stipulated delivery period is liable to pay ground rent for the period the material occupies railway premises.

q: A supplier offers an item with a local content of 60 per cent in a stores tender governed by the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order. The supplier is classified as a:
e: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a supplier with local content of 50 per cent or more, here 60 per cent, is a Class-I local supplier.

q: A railway is planning its annual procurement of goods and services. The minimum percentage of such procurement required to be made from Micro and Small Enterprises (MSMEs) is:
e: The prescribed minimum procurement from Micro and Small Enterprises is 25 per cent of annual procurement of goods and services.

q: A firm registered with NSIC/MSME participates in a stores tender invited by the Railways. As a rule, such a firm is exempted from payment of:
e: Firms registered with NSIC or as MSMEs are, as a rule, exempted from payment of Earnest Money Deposit in stores tenders.

q: In framing the Stores Budget, the value of stores to be drawn for works and maintenance is provided for in the estimates of those works and programmes. To prevent the same requirement being provided for twice, the Stores Budget carries a:
e: The Stores Budget carries a deduct entry so that stores requirements already provided for in works and maintenance estimates are not provided for twice.

q: Stores are issued from a depot for the day-to-day maintenance of a service, and the value of the issue is to be charged to revenue (working expenses). The Primary Unit linked with such issues of stores to revenue heads is:
e: Issues of stores from stock to revenue heads are charged under Primary Unit 27, the primary unit linked with the cost of materials from stock for working expenses.
